sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C,Kaushalendra Nath Singh Hon'ble Siddhartha Varma,J.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.The petitioners case is that as per the notification under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894, the State Government had acquired out of plot no. 279 rakba 2-13-10 of land actually.
Further from the plot no. 280 rakba 2-6-10 land was acquired.

2.Grievance of the petitioners is that instead of taking over the possession of the whole land from plot no. 279, rakba 1-14-0 has been taken and out of plot no. 280, rakba 1-19-0 has been taken.
3.Further grievance of the petitioners is that either the complete possession of plots no. 279 and 280 be taken over and compensation be paid or for the remaining land over which possession has been Brijesh Kumar And 8 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196031453/
1 taken without acquisition be released.

entities.text: Brijesh Kumar And 8 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4.In this regard, learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon a judgement of the Supreme court dated 20.1.2021 passed in SLP No. 6597 of 2017 (Nayan Tara vs. State of U.P. and others).

entities.text: Nayan Tara vs. State of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5.Learned counsel for the Noida Authorities, the respondent no. 2, states that if the petitioners file representations ventilating their grievances, the Noida Authority would look into the same.

6.Under such circumstances, we direct that if the petitioners file representations within a period of two weeks from today then the same shall be considered and decided in accordance with law within a period of one month thereafter.
7.With these observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
